messages:
sre-bot: ALERT: Elevated 500/timeout errors from tenant helix-77 on dedicated-eu-central-1-helix. error-rate=18% over 5m, queue_depth=420. Paging oncall.

eli: got the page. starting triage.

renee: customer HelixCorp reported truncated chat responses during longer context sessions. sample request id=abc123 shows a mid-stream cutoff.

devon: logs show repeated kernel OOMs on q4b-int8 instances and a surge in prefix cache evictions. Metric: kv_cache_hit drops from 97% -> 45%.

eli: hypothesis: quantized model variant q4b-int8 is thrashing under long context; dedicated pool lacks headroom due to recent increase in batch_size for that tenant. Mitigation: temporarily pin tenant to redwood/gpt-7b-safe:stable, enable hosted fallback, and reduce per-req max_tokens to 1024 for the tenant via config override.

renee: agree. Also want to avoid routing churn. Plan: 1) apply tenant model pin 2) add routing preference hosted with 15m ttl 3) enforce per-tenant request caps so we don't exhaust KV memory 4) inform HelixCorp support and schedule follow-up.

eng-runtime-bot: queued action apply-tenant-pin(helix-77)-> started

(terminal)
$ rictl tenant update --tenant-id helix-77 --model-pin redwood/gpt-7b-safe:stable --reason "incident mitigation - KV thrash"
Applying model pin... OK. pinned_model: redwood/gpt-7b-safe:stable

eng-runtime-bot: routing change applied: add fallback=hosted prefer=latency ttl=900s for tenant helix-77

(terminal)
$ rictl tenant config set --tenant-id helix-77 --max-tokens 1024 --reason "mitigation"
Updating config... OK.

devon: metrics: error-rate falling to 3% within 2m, p50 latency increased ~30ms, p95 unchanged. queue_depth back to ~45. KV hit_rate recovering.

support-bot: HelixCorp notified: "We've pinned your tenant to a safer model variant and temporarily routed requests to hosted fallback. You may see slightly higher latency but fewer truncations. We're monitoring and will follow up." Customer acknowledged.

eli: now applying pool soft-isolation to prevent cross-tenant bursts while we root-cause. Command: `rictl pool update --pool dedicated-eu-central-1-helix --isolation soft --retain-capacity 2`

eng-runtime-bot: pool isolation command executed.

renee: logging mitigation steps in incident INC-2026-058-helix. owners: eng-runtime, sres, account-ops. Adding follow-up tasks: re-qualify q4b-int8 under longer context, run KV-cache stress tests, add tenant warm-up hook.

devon: note on billing: hosted fallback is billed per normal hosted pricing. Mark incident usage as creditable if HelixCorp requests compensations; ping billing.

eli: handoff plan: i'll monitor for 45m then hand to night SRE. If error-rate <5% and queue_depth stable, we start a canary rollback: remove model-pin for 1% of traffic then 10% then full.

renee: saved commands and graphs to incident doc. adding playbook snippet here for future runs:
```
# emergency tenant mitigation
rictl tenant update --tenant-id <tenant> --model-pin <model:tag> --reason "incident mitigation"
rictl routing add --tenant <tenant> --policy "fallback=hosted,prefer=latency" --ttl 900
rictl tenant config set --tenant-id <tenant> --max-tokens <n>
rictl pool update --pool <pool> --isolation soft --retain-capacity <n>
# verify
rictl tenant status --tenant-id <tenant>
# rollback plan
rictl tenant update --tenant-id <tenant> --remove-model-pin
```
eng-runtime-bot: mitigation window set: 15m routing TTL + tenant pin. monitor job running.

eli: creating calendar invite for post-incident sync with HelixCorp ops at 11:00 CET.

devon: filing root-cause hypotheses: a) quantized kernel eviction pattern with long ctx b) bad batch sizing from recent client-side change c) subtle mem leak in q4b-int8 runtime path. Tests: repro harness with long sequences + elevated batch concurrency.

renee: adding SLO item: enterprise tenants with dedicated pools should have a KV cache headroom metric and alert before saturation.

support-bot: PAGE CLOSED by eli at 2026-03-14T00:51Z

eli: final notes: mitigation successful, customer impact reduced to background errors. we'll keep pin+fallback for 2 hours, then run controlled canary rollback. postmortem to follow with RCA and next steps.
summary: HelixCorp (tenant helix-77) experienced elevated 500s/timeouts on dedicated pool due to KV-cache thrash and quantized instance memory pressure. Team pinned tenant to safe model, routed to hosted fallback with TTL, reduced max_tokens, applied soft pool isolation, monitored recovery, and scheduled follow-ups for requalification and SLO improvements.
